draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Khandala! It's one half of the twin hill stations of Lonavala and Khandala, and the Kune Falls close by is counted as the 14th highest waterfall in India.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat in my notes for Khandala, so ask around near the station for whatever's fresh today.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Khandala railway station is barely a minute's walk away, and Kune Falls is about 16 minutes on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Walk over to Kune Falls and just sit and watch the water come down the hillside for a while.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Khandala station is where the Khandala Ghat begins, the climb down the hills towards Mumbai starts right after it.

tips.title: Use the train from Lonavala.
tips.body: Khandala is the very next station towards Pune from Lonavala, where the Pune Suburban Service starts.

tips.title: Keep the waterfall for daylight.
tips.body: Kune Falls is a waterfall on a hillside, so go while it's light and you can see the path.

story.title: Twin hill stations
story.body: Khandala sits in Pune district, paired with Lonavala as twin hill stations. The two towns share the same stretch of the Western Ghats.

story.title: Top of the ghat
story.body: Khandala railway station, code KAD, has three platforms. Heading towards Mumbai, the Khandala Ghat starts right after it.

story.title: Waterfall country
story.body: Kune Falls at Khandala is ranked the 14th highest waterfall in India. It's the big natural draw of the town.
